title: Linear Single-Source Shortest Path, Almost
summary: We give a comparison-addition algorithm for single-source shortest paths in undirected graphs with nonnegative real edge lengths. For each input with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, its expected running time is $O(m+n\log\log\log n)$. It terminates almost surely. Every terminating run returns exact distances and a shortest-path tree on the reachable vertices. The bound is independent of the ratio of edge lengths and is linear whenever $m=Ω(n\log\log\log n)$.
